title: One of the first Black players with an electric guitar
summary: He says he was among the first Black musicians with an electric guitar, played it on the boat band in New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: That's when you were playing the guitar mainly. Yeah. And I gather you had one of the first amplified guitars in the area.
Well, when I get to all Bart Chubb, I was probably one of the first black to have an electric guitar.

Yeah. Well, other fellas came after, they weren't safe that way. But they had a lot of white musicians had an electric guitar. Because I was dealing with the wheel line from way back then, in the late 20s and all through the 30s and things like that, up to today.
When did you start playing the electric guitar? In Chicago or on the uh?

No, I was working in New Orleans. Oh. In New Orleans, yeah. I worked in this band, had electric guitar. Yeah. A couple of other guys got them out to meet. Kimmel Garfunkel and A.J. Monner and a couple of other fellas. George Gainer.
What sort of music were you playing at that, you know, when you were playing there?
Well, at that time I said those were in ten piece bands.
Oh, so you were playing the electric guitar in the ten piece band?

And the band, yeah, yeah. Just about the last, before, the 38, the last two years, the captain told me, you don't need the band, you know, most everybody wants to listen to electric guitar now. So for that two years I didn't play it on the boom. So you were playing the guitar in the boat? Yeah, but I didn't want to listen to the guitar because, you know, well, the band was going out as far as those kinds of bands, you see. Banjo was going out.
